creator: main-context
purpose: Establish REAL token measurements for formula tuning
mission_goal: Measure actual token burn vs. theoretical predictions. Establish baseline for mutation→eval cycle.

phase_1_baseline_measurement.goal: Measure W1 spawn cost under different context fills

tasks.description: Spawn 4 agents at context=70%, record /usage delta, compare to theory
measurement_points: Theory predicted: 5K tokens for W1 light bundle × 4 agents

tasks.description: Same as above but at context=60% (earlier spawn = more available runtime)
Measure: What does it cost to inject NECTAR.md into bundle?
method: Render bundle WITHOUT NECTAR
Measure: bundle size, agent prompt size
Render bundle WITH NECTAR (full 97KB)
Measure: bundle size delta
Estimate: NECTAR injection cost to agent context

tasks.description: Same as NECTAR but for HONEY.md
method: Render bundle WITH global HONEY (62KB)
Render bundle WITH global + project HONEY (if exists)
Measure size delta + agent prompt size impact

phase_2_formula_calibration.goal: Use real measurements to calibrate theoretical formulas

tasks.description: Do the wave thresholds (70%, 80%, 87%) actually predict agent behavior?
method: Hypothesis: At context=70%, agents complete fast enough to hit cache TTL (5min)
Test: Spawn 4 agents at 70%, measure actual runtime vs. 5min target
If actual runtime = 3.5min → agents finish before cache TTL (good!)
If actual runtime = 7min → miss cache TTL (need to spawn earlier)
Iterate: Adjust WAVE_1_SPAWN_MAX_CONTEXT_PCT formula based on real runtime data

tasks.description: Does burn_rate = (delta_pct / delta_sec) * 60 actually predict compact timing?
method: Measurement: Track altimeter.json across 3 sessions, collect (context%, timestamp) pairs
Compute observed burn_rate_pct_per_min from each pair
Theory: time_to_compact = (93.5 - curr_pct) / burn_rate
Actual: Does compact fire when predicted?
Gap analysis: If formula predicts 45min but compact fires at 30min → burn_rate calculation wrong

tasks.description: Do quality_score thresholds (0.50, 0.70, 0.80, 0.85) actually gate work as intended?
method: Collect all manifests from past 7 days, extract quality_score values
Histogram: How many tasks have quality 0.50-0.60? 0.60-0.70? etc.
Theory: DEEPEN gate at 0.70 should reject ~10-15% of tasks
Actual: What % of tasks are BLOCKED at 0.70 gate?
If actual << 10%, gate is too lenient. If actual >> 15%, gate is too strict.

tasks.description: Do reputation_weight values (0.35 truthfulness, 0.30 depth, etc.) actually drive agent behavior?
method: Collect 20 agents with different composite_scores (0.4, 0.6, 0.8, etc.)
Observation: Do agents with score <0.5 actually get constrained to retraining work?
Observation: Do agents with score >0.75 get harder missions?
If yes → weights are well-calibrated. If no → adjust weights.

phase_3_eval_wiring.goal: Wire real measurements into /dev-eval + /metrics for continuous monitoring

tasks.description: Every spawn should log actual token consumption to metrics-ledger.jsonl
Presend hook should flag if /spawn violates context gates (as you just discovered!)

spec.check: If context_pct > WAVE_3_SPAWN_MAX_CONTEXT_PCT, warn: 'HIGH CONTEXT, W3 BACKGROUND ONLY'
If context_pct > 93.5, error: 'CONTEXT RED ALERT, COMPACT IMMINENT, DON'T SPAWN'

tasks.description: Track: Do agents do more than assigned? Do they emit bundles? Do droplets get cited?

metrics: droplet_cross_citations (how many agents cited droplets in manifests)
context_leverage (% of agent context spent on discovery vs. primary task)

how_to_use_this_bundle.description: This is NOT a task list for one agent. This is a MISSION CONTEXT for 3-4 agents to tackle in parallel.
phases: Phase 1 (W1 LIFTOFF): Spawn 3-4 agents in parallel on different measurement tasks. Each measures one formula aspect.
Phase 2 (W2 CRUISE): When Phase 1 results return, spawn synthesizer to cross-correlate and identify gaps.
Phase 3 (W3 INSERTION): Background agent wires findings into /dev-eval + /metrics.
Phase 4 (Main): You read results, decide which formulas need calibration, commit changes.
